controls.poles_zeros.title: Poles, zeros and system type of a transfer function

variables.name: poles
variables.desc: poles (characteristic-equation roots) as [real, imag] pairs, sorted

variables.name: gain
variables.desc: transfer-function gain k from scipy tf2zpk (signed: k can be negative)

variables.name: type
variables.desc: system type (number of open-loop poles at the origin)

assumptions: The characteristic equation is den(s) = 0; its roots are the poles. A pole with positive real part means the open loop is unstable.

controls.block_reduction.title: Block-diagram reduction (series / parallel / feedback)

variables.name: setup
variables.desc: {"num1","den1","num2","den2","conn"} with conn series | parallel | feedback (negative) | feedback_pos

assumptions: Two-block reduction: series G1·G2, parallel G1 + G2, feedback G1/(1 ± G1·G2). Common pole/zero factors are not cancelled (use poles_zeros to inspect).

controls.second_order_step.title: Second-order step response metrics (damping ratio and natural frequency)
assumptions: Standard underdamped second-order step response, 0 < ζ < 1. Settling uses the 2 % criterion t_s = 4/(ζωn); the rise-time formula is the 0–100 % definition.
method_references: Second-order step metrics: tp = π/ωd; %OS = 100 e^(−ζπ/√(1−ζ²)); ts = 4/(ζωn) (2 % criterion)

controls.steady_state_error.title: System type, error constants and steady-state errors

procedure.python:
def _ss_error(v):
    """System type, static error constants and steady-state errors from the open-loop G(s) = num/den.

    Type N = number of poles at the origin (trailing zero coefficients in den). With K = N(0)/D_red(0):
    Kp = K (N=0) else ∞; Kv = 0 (N=0), K (N=1), ∞ (N≥2); Ka = 0 (N≤1), K (N=2), ∞ (N>2). Steady-state
    errors: e_step = 1/(1+Kp); e_ramp = 1/Kv; e_para = 1/Ka. An infinite error is reported as null.
    """
    num, den = _coeffs(v['num'], 'num'), _coeffs(v['den'], 'den')
    if den[0] == 0:
        raise MechError('den: leading coefficient must be non-zero')
    # Cancel common factors of s at the origin (pole-zero cancellation at s = 0) so a zero open-loop
    # error constant is reported as an infinite error instead of dividing by zero.
    while len(num) > 1 and len(den) > 1 and num[-1] == 0.0 and den[-1] == 0.0:
        num.pop()
        den.pop()
    t = 0
    while t < len(den) and den[len(den) - 1 - t] == 0.0:
        t += 1
    red = den[:len(den) - t]  # remove the s^N factor
    n0 = num[-1] if num else 0.0
    d0 = red[-1] if red else 1.0
    if d0 == 0.0:
        raise MechError('den: constant term is zero after removing the s^N factor')
    K = n0 / d0
    Kp = K if t == 0 else None
    Kv = K if t == 1 else (0.0 if t == 0 else None)
    Ka = K if t == 2 else (0.0 if t < 2 else None)
    e_step = (1.0 / (1.0 + K)) if (t == 0 and 1.0 + K != 0.0) else (0.0 if t > 0 else None)
    e_ramp = (1.0 / K) if (t == 1 and K != 0.0) else (None if t == 0 else 0.0)
    e_para = (1.0 / K) if (t == 2 and K != 0.0) else (None if t < 2 else 0.0)
    return {'result': {'type': t, 'Kp': Kp, 'Kv': Kv, 'Ka': Ka,
                       'e_step': e_step, 'e_ramp': e_ramp, 'e_para': e_para}}

assumptions: Unity feedback, unit test inputs. e_step = 1/(1+Kp), e_ramp = 1/Kv, e_para = 1/Ka. Infinite error/constant is reported as null (e.g. a type-0 system tracking a ramp).
method_references: Static error constants Kp, Kv, Ka; steady-state errors

controls.routh_hurwitz.title: Routh–Hurwitz stability of a characteristic polynomial

variables.name: stable
variables.desc: 1 if all roots are strictly in the left half-plane, else 0

variables.name: marginal
variables.desc: 1 if no RHP roots but roots on the imaginary axis (repeated jω roots are in fact unstable)

variables.name: n_imag
variables.desc: number of roots on the imaginary axis (from the auxiliary polynomial)

variables.name: first_column
variables.desc: first column of the Routh array (ε → 0 limit; null where unbounded)

variables.name: routh_table
variables.desc: Routh array rows (ε → 0 limit; padded with zeros)

procedure.python:
def _routh(v):
    """Routh–Hurwitz stability of the characteristic polynomial (descending coefficients).

    Builds the Routh array exactly (sympy rationals). A zero first-column entry with a non-zero row is
    replaced by ε and the first column is read in the limit ε → 0⁺; an all-zero row is replaced by the
    derivative of the auxiliary polynomial and signals marginal stability (roots on the imaginary axis).
    Sign changes in the first column equal the number of right-half-plane roots.
    """
    coeffs = _coeffs(v['coeffs'], 'coeffs')
    if coeffs[0] == 0.0:
        raise MechError('coeffs: leading coefficient must be non-zero')
    a0 = coeffs[0]
    coeffs = [c / a0 for c in coeffs]  # monic: does not change stability
    n = len(coeffs) - 1
    eps = sp.Symbol('_eps', positive=True)
    r0 = [sp.Rational(c) for c in coeffs[0::2]]
    r1 = [sp.Rational(c) for c in coeffs[1::2]]
    L = len(r0)
    r0 += [sp.Integer(0)] * (L - len(r0))
    r1 += [sp.Integer(0)] * (L - len(r1))
    rows = [r0, r1]
    n_imag = 0          # roots exactly on the imaginary axis, from the first auxiliary polynomial
    while len(rows) <= n:
        prev, prev2 = rows[-1], rows[-2]
        if all(x == 0 for x in prev):
            # All-zero row: replace it with the derivative of the auxiliary polynomial built from the
            # row above (prev2); signals roots on the imaginary axis (marginal stability).
            m = n - len(rows) + 2  # s-power associated with the row above
            # An all-zero row only says the polynomial has root pairs symmetric about the origin; they may be
            # ±jω (imaginary axis), ±σ (real) or quadruples. Count the imaginary-axis ones from the auxiliary
            # polynomial's roots instead of assuming all are on the axis (review of brief 22f: s²−1, s⁴+1).
            if n_imag == 0:
                aux = [0.0] * (m + 1)  # descending powers s^m … s^0
                for j in range(len(prev2)):
                    if m - 2 * j >= 0:
                        aux[2 * j] = float(prev2[j])
                roots = np.roots(aux)
                scale = max(1.0, max((abs(r) for r in roots), default=1.0))
                n_imag = int(sum(1 for r in roots if abs(r.real) <= 1e-7 * scale))
            der = [sp.Integer(0)] * L
            for j in range(len(prev2)):
                p = m - 2 * j
                if p > 0:
                    der[j] = p * prev2[j]
            if all(x == 0 for x in der):
                raise MechError('Routh table has a degenerate auxiliary polynomial; cannot decide stability')
            rows[-1] = der
            continue  # do not grow: the next pass computes the following row from the derivative
        pivot = prev[0]
        if pivot == 0:
            prev[0] = eps  # zero first-column entry (non-zero row): epsilon substitution
            pivot = eps
        new = [sp.Integer(0)] * L
        for j in range(L - 1):
            new[j] = sp.together((prev[0] * prev2[j + 1] - prev2[0] * prev[j + 1]) / pivot)
        rows.append(new)

    first = [r[0] for r in rows]
    signs = []
    for x in first:
        s = _sign_limit(x, eps)
        if s == 0:
            raise MechError('Routh table has an unresolved zero in the first column; cannot decide stability')
        signs.append(s)
    n_rhp = sum(1 for i in range(1, len(signs)) if signs[i] != signs[i - 1])
    marginal = n_rhp == 0 and n_imag > 0
    stable = 1 if (n_rhp == 0 and n_imag == 0) else 0
    first_column = [_as_float(x, eps) for x in first]
    table = [[_as_float(x, eps) for x in row] for row in rows]
    return {'n_rhp': n_rhp, 'stable': stable, 'marginal': 1 if marginal else 0, 'n_imag': n_imag,
            'first_column': first_column, 'routh_table': table}

assumptions: Sign changes in the first column equal the number of RHP roots (Routh–Hurwitz). A zero first-column entry is handled by the ε → 0 limit; an all-zero row is replaced by the derivative of the auxiliary polynomial and signals marginal stability.

controls.freq_response.title: Frequency response magnitude and phase at one frequency (Bode)

variables.name: phase
variables.desc: continuous phase of G(jω) (sum of zero angles minus pole angles)

assumptions: Single frequency point; use the bode plot for a sweep. Phase is the continuous (unwrapped) angle built as the sum of zero angles minus pole angles, so it keeps decreasing through −180° instead of wrapping to +180°.

controls.root_locus.title: Closed-loop poles at a gain (root locus)

variables.name: closed_poles
variables.desc: roots of den + K·num as [real, imag] pairs, sorted

assumptions: Negative unity feedback: closed-loop characteristic equation den + K·num = 0. The locus chart sweeps K about the given value; branches are drawn as pole trajectories.

controls.stability_margins.title: Gain margin, phase margin, crossover frequencies and bandwidth

variables.name: gain_margin
variables.desc: gain margin in dB (null if undefined; negative for an unstable system)

variables.name: phase_margin
variables.desc: phase margin (null if undefined; negative for an unstable system)

variables.name: w_pc
variables.desc: phase-crossover frequency (∠G = −180°; null if the phase never crosses −180°)

variables.name: bandwidth
variables.desc: closed-loop −3 dB bandwidth of T = G/(1+G) (null if DC gain is zero or infinite)

assumptions: Open-loop frequency response with a continuous (unwrapped) phase. Margins are taken from genuine crossings: a phase pinned at −180° (e.g. a double integrator) has no phase crossover, so gain margin and ω_pc are null. Bandwidth is the closed-loop T = G/(1+G) −3 dB frequency.
method_references: Gain/phase margin definitions from the Bode plot

controls.pid_ziegler_nichols.title: Ziegler–Nichols PID gains from ultimate gain and period
assumptions: Closed-loop Ziegler–Nichols (ultimate-sensitivity) method: P Kp = 0.5 K_u; PI Kp = 0.45 K_u, Ti = T_u/1.2; PID Kp = 0.6 K_u, Ti = T_u/2, Td = T_u/8. These give a quarter-decay response; retune for your process.

controls.state_space.title: State-space eigenvalues, controllability and observability

variables.name: eigenvalues
variables.desc: eigenvalues (system poles) as [real, imag] pairs, sorted

assumptions: ẋ = A x + B u, y = C x. The feedthrough matrix D does not affect the eigenvalues, controllability or observability.

source.derivation: G = (s+1)/(s(s+2)): zero at −1; poles at 0 and −2; gain 1; one pole at the origin → type 1
G = −1/(s+1): no zeros, pole at −1, gain k = −1 (signed), no poles at the origin → type 0
unity negative feedback: G = (1/(s+1))/(1 + 1/(s+1)) = 1/(s+2)
type 0 (no pole at origin): Kp = G(0) = 10/2 = 5; e_step = 1/(1+5) = 1/6; Kv = Ka = 0 so ramp/parabola errors are infinite (null)
type 1: Kv = lim sG = 1/1 = 1; e_ramp = 1/Kv = 1; e_step = 0; Kp infinite (null); Ka = 0 so e_para infinite (null)

G = s/(s(s+1)) = 1/(s+1) after cancelling the common s factor: type 0, Kp = G(0) = 1, e_step = 1/(1+1) = 0.5, Kv = Ka = 0 so ramp/parabola errors infinite (null). Cancelling the s factors first avoids dividing by the zero error constant.
s³+6s²+11s+6 = (s+1)(s+2)(s+3): Routh first column [1, 6, (6·11−1·6)/6 = 10, 6] → no sign changes → stable
s³+s²+2s+8 = (s+2)(s²−s+4): Routh first column [1, 1, (1·2−1·8)/1 = −6, 8] → two sign changes → two RHP roots
s⁵+2s⁴+2s³+4s²+11s+10 has a zero first-column pivot (ε substitution); numpy.roots gives 0.895±1.456j (RHP pair), −1.241±1.038j, −1.309 → two RHP roots
s³+s+1: zero s² coefficient; Routh with ε gives first column [1, ε, (ε−1)/ε, 1] → signs +,+,−,+ → two sign changes; numpy.roots gives 0.341±1.162j (RHP pair), −0.682 → two RHP roots
s⁵+2s⁴+3s³+6s²+5s+3: first column [1, 2, ε, (6ε−7)/ε, 3.5, 3] → signs +,+,+,−,+,+ → two sign changes; numpy.roots gives 0.343±1.508j (RHP pair) → two RHP roots
s³+s²+s+1 = (s+1)(s²+1): all-zero row → auxiliary polynomial s²+1 with roots ±j on the imaginary axis → marginal (never strictly stable); numpy.roots gives −1, ±j
G = 1/(s+1)³: three poles at −1 give phase = −3·atan(ω) = −3·atan(3) = −3·1.2490458 = −3.7471373 rad (continuous, not wrapped to +2.536 rad); |G| = 1/(√(1+9))³ = 1/√1000 → −30 dB
|G| = 1/√(ω²+1) = 1/√2 → ω = 1 rad/s (inverse)
closed loop s²+2s+2 = 0 → s = −1 ± j

cases.classification: reference landmark; original citation confidence retained in source; not a certified external benchmark

source.ref: Phase margin of G = 1/(s(s+1)) is the classic 51.83° (recalled landmark): ω_gc solves ω²(ω²+1) = 1 → ω = 0.78615; PM = 180 − 90 − atan(0.78615) = 51.827°

source.derivation: closed loop T = G/(1+G) = 1/(s²+s+1); |T| = 1/√(ω⁴−ω²+1) = 1/√2 → ω⁴−ω²−1 = 0 → ω² = (1+√5)/2 → ω = √1.61803 = 1.27202 rad/s (closed-loop −3 dB bandwidth)

K = 6 is the critical gain of 1/(s(s+1)(s+2)): at ω = √2 the loop gain is exactly 1 and the phase −180°, so GM = 0 dB and PM = 0° (both margins zero at the stability limit; abs_tol covers the brentq round-off near the exact zero)

K = 10 exceeds the critical gain: the unwrapped phase at the gain crossover (ω_gc = 1.8022) is below −180°, giving PM = −12.997° = −0.226844 rad and GM = −4.436975 dB (both negative for the unstable loop)
G = 1/s² has ∠G = −180° everywhere (Im G ≡ 0), so the phase never crosses −180°: ω_pc and gain margin are undefined (null), not −320 dB at the first grid point; |G| = 1 at ω = 1 rad/s
Ki_PID = 1.2 K_u/T_u → K_u = 2.4·2/1.2 = 4 (inverse)
companion form of 1/(s²+3s+2): eigenvalues −1, −2; Ctrb = [B, AB] = [[0,1],[1,−3]] rank 2; Obsv = [C; CA] = [[1,0],[0,1]] rank 2 → controllable and observable
s² − 1 = (s − 1)(s + 1): roots ±1, one in the RHP, none on the imaginary axis (reviewer case, verify22f)
s⁴ + 1: roots e^{jπ(2k+1)/4} = (±1 ± j)/√2, two with positive real part, none on the axis (reviewer case)
s³ + s² + s + 1 = (s + 1)(s² + 1): roots −1, ±j → two on the imaginary axis, marginal
